Generate an augmented p-rep design

Source: R/augmented_prep.R
augmented_prep_design.Rd

Creates a multi-location augmented partially replicated (p-rep) design (Williams, Piepho and Whitaker, 2011). Instead of replicated checks, a subset of the test entries is replicated at each location: every entry is planted once at every location, and the entries chosen for p-rep at a location get extra plots there. All plots of a location are arranged in incomplete blocks, chosen so that pairs of entries share a block at most once across the whole trial ((0,1)-designs).

Usage

augmented_prep_design(
  treatments,
  locations,
  block_size = 8,
  prep_prop = NULL,
  n_duplicate_per_location = NULL,
  replications_per_repeated_entry = 2,
  n_blocks_per_location = NULL,
  resolvable = FALSE,
  n_candidates = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  field_cols = NULL,
  rows_per_block = NULL,
  blocks_per_row = NULL,
  serpentine = TRUE,
  output_file = NULL,
  method = c("search", "alpha", "alpha2"),
  n_prep_per_block = NULL,
  n_efficiency_candidates = 5
)

Arguments

treatments

Character vector of entry names.

locations

Character vector of location names.

block_size

Maximum final incomplete block size. Can be a single integer or a named vector indexed by location (the algebraic methods use its smallest value). Actual block sizes may differ by one plot when totals do not divide evenly.

prep_prop

Optional proportion of entries to duplicate per location (method = "search" only). If NULL, entries are split across locations so each entry is duplicated at approximately one location.

n_duplicate_per_location

Optional number of entries duplicated at each location (method = "search" only). Can be a single integer, a vector matching locations, or a named vector indexed by location.

replications_per_repeated_entry

Total number of plots for entries selected for p-rep replication at a location. The default 2 gives one base plot plus one extra plot. Can be a single integer or a named vector indexed by location. Must be 2 for the algebraic methods.

n_blocks_per_location

Optional number of incomplete blocks at each location (method = "search" only). If NULL, the number of blocks is the minimum needed so no block is larger than block_size. Can be a single integer or a named vector indexed by location.

resolvable

Logical (method = "search"). If TRUE, each location is laid out as a resolvable design: the blocks are grouped into replications_per_repeated_entry replicates, each replicate holds every p-rep entry of that location exactly once plus an even share of the unreplicated entries, and all replicates have the same number of blocks. If n_blocks_per_location is given it must be a multiple of the number of replicates. Designs from the algebraic methods are always resolvable.

n_candidates

Maximum number of candidate designs ("search") or of random starting arrays ("alpha", "alpha2") to generate. summary$n_candidates_evaluated reports how many were used.

seed

Optional random seed.

field_cols

Optional number of field columns for row/column layout. Can be a single integer or a named vector indexed by location.

rows_per_block

Optional number of physical field rows each incomplete block should occupy. Can be a single integer or a named vector for selected locations. Must be used with blocks_per_row for those locations.

blocks_per_row

Optional number of incomplete blocks to place side by side in each field row band. Can be a single integer or a named vector for selected locations. Must be used with rows_per_block for those locations.

serpentine

Logical. If TRUE, row/column coordinates use serpentine ordering within each location.

output_file

Optional tab-delimited output file for the complete design.

method

Construction method: "search", "alpha" or "alpha2" (see Details).

n_prep_per_block

For the algebraic methods, the number m of p-rep entries in every block. If NULL, the largest feasible m whose blocks fit in block_size is used.

n_efficiency_candidates

Number of optimal candidates (no entry repeated within a block, connected locations, and no pair of entries sharing more than one block) to compare on the average efficiency factor; the one with the highest efficiency is returned. Use 1 to return the first optimal candidate. Efficiency is compared for up to 2000 entries.

Value

A list with design inputs, summary diagnostics, complete plot-level design, Breedbase-compatible design columns, block summary, replication summary, repeated-entry groups, and pairwise concurrence matrix. In the complete design, repeated_at is the location where the entry receives its extra p-rep plot(s), or "not_repeated" when the entry is not selected for extra replication. replicate is the replicate (superblock) of the plot for resolvable designs, and 1 otherwise; the Breedbase rep column is replicate for resolvable designs and the plot's occurrence number otherwise.

Details

Three construction methods are available through method:

"search" (default)

A flexible randomized search. Any number of entries, locations, block sizes, p-rep proportions (prep_prop, n_duplicate_per_location), replication levels (replications_per_repeated_entry) and block counts can be used, with an optional resolvable layout (resolvable).

"alpha"

The partial alpha-array construction of Section 2.1 of the paper. An alpha-array for l * m rows and 2l replicates is searched, the m x 2 rectangles on its diagonal give the two-replicate design for the p-rep entries of each location, and half of the remaining elements of each column are deleted (Section 2.2) so that the design is a (0,1)-design. Every entry is duplicated at exactly one location, each location is resolvable with two replicates of s blocks, and each block holds m p-rep entries; the final block size is (l + 1) m / 2 (blocks of the two replicates differ by one plot when this is not an integer).

"alpha2"

The augmented alpha(2)-array construction of Section 2.4, for even m and an odd number of blocks per replicate s. Every block has (l + 1) m / 2 plots.

For the algebraic methods, m is set with n_prep_per_block (or chosen as the largest value whose blocks fit in block_size), the number of blocks and of duplicated entries follow from the construction, and replications_per_repeated_entry must be 2. When the number of entries is not a multiple of the array size, the surplus array positions are dropped as dummy entries, so some blocks are one plot smaller. augmented_prep_parameters() lists the feasible parameter sets.

The incomplete block structure is independent from the field geometry. By default, field_cols lays the ordered plots into rows and columns. For a rectangular block layout, use rows_per_block and blocks_per_row to place multiple blocks side by side within each location.

With method = "search", the p-rep plots of every location are spread evenly over its blocks, and the p-rep entries are placed so that they link all blocks of the location (the location is connected), so entry effects can also be estimated from each location on its own. A warning is given when there are too few p-rep plots to connect the blocks. After the random greedy search, the best candidates are improved by swapping plots between blocks to remove pairs of entries that share more than one block.

For all methods, summary reports the maximum pairwise concurrence, the number of locations whose blocks are not connected, and the average efficiency factor efficiency_factor of the block design (Section 2.3 of the paper; higher is better), which can be used to compare designs. Entry labels, block order within replicates and plot order within blocks are randomized.

References

Williams, E., Piepho, H.-P. and Whitaker, D. (2011). Augmented p-rep designs. Biometrical Journal 53, 19-27. doi:10.1002/bimj.201000102

See also

augmented_prep_parameters(), analyze_augmented_prep_design(), plot_augmented_prep_design()

Examples

design <- augmented_prep_design(
  treatments = paste0("G", seq_len(12)),
  locations = c("Loc1", "Loc2", "Loc3"),
  block_size = c(Loc1 = 5, Loc2 = 5, Loc3 = 6),
  n_blocks_per_location = c(Loc1 = 4, Loc2 = 4, Loc3 = 4),
  n_duplicate_per_location = c(Loc1 = 4, Loc2 = 2, Loc3 = 4),
  replications_per_repeated_entry = c(Loc1 = 2, Loc2 = 3, Loc3 = 2),
  n_candidates = 5,
  seed = 123,
  field_cols = 8
)

design$summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 20
#>       score max_pairwise_concurr…¹ n_pairs_with_concurr…² total_excess_concurr…³
#>       <dbl>                  <int>                  <int>                  <dbl>
#> 1 130002004                      2                     13                     13
#> # ℹ abbreviated names: ¹​max_pairwise_concurrence,
#> #   ²​n_pairs_with_concurrence_gt_1, ³​total_excess_concurrence
#> # ℹ 16 more variables: same_entry_same_block <dbl>,
#> #   n_disconnected_locations <int>, efficiency_factor <dbl>, resolvable <lgl>,
#> #   min_replication <int>, max_replication <int>, mean_replication <dbl>,
#> #   n_locations <int>, n_entries <int>, n_plots <int>, n_blocks <int>,
#> #   n_candidates_evaluated <int>, method <chr>, m <int>, s <int>, …
head(design$design)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 16
#>   plots location   row   col replicate block block_uid block_size plot_in_block
#>   <int> <chr>    <dbl> <int>     <int> <int> <chr>          <int>         <int>
#> 1     1 Loc1         1     1         1     1 Loc1_B001          4             1
#> 2     2 Loc1         1     2         1     1 Loc1_B001          4             2
#> 3     3 Loc1         1     3         1     1 Loc1_B001          4             3
#> 4     4 Loc1         1     4         1     1 Loc1_B001          4             4
#> 5     5 Loc1         1     5         1     2 Loc1_B002          4             1
#> 6     6 Loc1         1     6         1     2 Loc1_B002          4             2
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: all_entries <chr>, occurrence <int>, entry_type <chr>,
#> #   is_extra_repeat <int>, repeated_at <chr>, rep <int>, is_control <int>

# Example 1 of Williams, Piepho and Whitaker (2011): 20 entries, two
# locations, blocks of 3 built from a partial alpha-array.
alpha <- augmented_prep_design(
  treatments = paste0("G", 1:20),
  locations = c("L1", "L2"),
  method = "alpha",
  block_size = 3,
  seed = 1
)
alpha$summary[, c("method", "m", "s", "max_pairwise_concurrence", "efficiency_factor")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   method     m     s max_pairwise_concurrence efficiency_factor
#>   <chr>  <int> <int>                    <int>             <dbl>
#> 1 alpha      2     5                        1             0.609
